value.first: I'd use the Ferber method (graduated check-ins), with her in her own crib in her room. It's one of the best-studied sleep methods there is, and follow-ups found no harm to attachment or behaviour. If she's in a toddler bed, not a crib, use the chair method instead, since she can follow you out. Pick a clear week, same bedtime 6:30-8:00, a 20-30 minute bath, book, bed routine in her room, then down awake, goodnight phrase, leave.
value.second: Nights 1-3: when she cries, wait 3 min, then 5, then 10 (night 2: 5/10/12, night 3: 10/12/15). Checks are 1-2 min, lights off, same phrase, then leave. No pickup, and never bring her back to your bed; treat 2am wakings the same way. Expect 30-60+ min of protest, and night 2 or 3 worse than night 1. That spike is the old habit breaking. Nights 4-7: keep stretching, up to 20/25/30 by night 7.
value.third: It's working when she falls asleep faster each night; many kids are down in minutes by the end of the week. Pick who does checks each night so nobody caves, and never lock or hold her door shut. If she snores, gasps, or pauses breathing in her sleep, that's worth a call to her doctor.
